data.body:
CI FAILED ON 1336 WITH Verified-1, AND IT WAS THE STALE-BASE TRAP, NOT A DEFECT IN THE CHANGE. Diagnosed rather than guessed, and the diagnosis is worth recording because the failure is indistinguishable from a real one by its label.

THE FAILING STEP: 'build-and-test (gate + suite on the patchset) / lint + type-check' -> step 'wall-clock-assert gate' (run 30869375084). Every other job succeeded.

THE CAUSE. The step runs 'python scripts/check_wall_clock_asserts.py'. That script DID NOT EXIST in the change's tree: the change was based on 6739ea54fa, and the gate arrived on main afterwards with '1e95: gate upper-bound wall-clock asserts in tests'. Verified both sides directly — 'git show HEAD~1:scripts/check_wall_clock_asserts.py' fails, 'git show origin/main:scripts/check_wall_clock_asserts.py' succeeds. Gerrit CI runs the TARGET BRANCH's workflow against the patchset's tree, so main's workflow invoked a script the patchset did not have and the step failed on a missing file. Nothing in this change violates the gate.

THE FIX WAS A REBASE, not a code change. Rebased onto current origin/main f83fe24749 (main had advanced twice more while 1336 sat in review): new HEAD 71e2adcfdd, Change-Id preserved, tree clean. The previously-failing gate now runs and reports 'wall-clock-asserts: clean', exit 0. Re-pushed as a new patchset on 1336.

A FINDING THAT MATTERS BEYOND THIS CHANGE: THERE ARE EIGHT CI-ONLY GATE SCRIPTS, and the gate checklist this session inherited named only two of them. From .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:
    check_comment_hygiene.py      check_config_reads.py       check_docs_index.py
    check_raw_git_writes.py       check_readme_quickstart.py  check_server_manifest.py
    check_verify_gate_parity.py   check_wall_clock_asserts.py
NONE of these is in the Makefile, so 'make lint' does not cover any of them, and a contributor or agent running the documented five-gate sequence can push something CI will reject — which is exactly what happened here. I have now run ALL EIGHT against the rebased tree and every one exits 0:
    wall_clock_asserts 0 | comment_hygiene 0 | config_reads 0 | docs_index 0
    raw_git_writes 0 | readme_quickstart 0 | server_manifest 0 | verify_gate_parity 0
plus make lint 0, make typecheck 0, gen_env_registry --check 0, and the change's own 4 tests green. The full offline suite is re-running against the rebased tree because the rebase pulled in main commits between 6739ea54fa and f83fe24749 that this change's config flip could interact with — a new test resolving LLM config would be the realistic failure — so the earlier 9808-passed run is NOT being cited for the rebased artifact.

TWO GENERALISABLE LESSONS, recorded because both cost time today. (1) A Verified-1 whose step is a GATE SCRIPT should be checked for the script's EXISTENCE in the tree before its output is read as a violation; the handoff warned 'rebase before diagnosing any CI failure you cannot reproduce locally' and this is that case exactly. (2) The authoritative gate list is the WORKFLOW FILE, not the Makefile and not prose documentation — the two have drifted, and only the workflow gates a landing.
